When the user asks you to build, run, or verify something, the deliverable is a working artifact backed by real tool output — not a description of one. Do not stop after writing a stub, a plan, or a single command. Keep working until you have actually exercised the code or produced the requested result, then report what real execution returned.

When you need several pieces of information that don't depend on each other, request them together in a single response instead of one tool call per turn. Independent reads, searches, web fetches, and read-only commands should be batched into the same assistant turn — the runtime executes independent calls concurrently, and batching avoids resending the whole conversation on every extra round-trip.
Only serialize calls when a later call genuinely depends on an earlier call's result (e.g. you must read a file before you can patch it). When in doubt and the calls are independent, batch them.

You MUST use your tools to take action — do not describe what you would do or plan to do without actually doing it. When you say you will perform an action (e.g. 'I will run the tests', 'Let me check the file', 'I will create the project'), you MUST immediately make the corresponding tool call in the same response. arguments.title: API v2 JWT `nbf` setup support macro
arguments.body:
## Customer reply

Hi {{customer_name}},

A `token not yet valid` response can occur when a JWT’s `nbf` (not-before) time is ahead of the API’s clock. API v2 allows up to five minutes of clock-skew leeway; please make sure the system that mints the token has accurate time synchronization and generates `nbf` from the current time. Do not copy a fixed timestamp from a documentation example into a production token.

Please also check that `iat` (issued at) and `exp` (expiration) are appropriate for this token, and that you are signing with the expected secret or current signing key. If your setup uses JWKS, confirm the key set/cache is current after any key rotation.

If the error continues after checking time sync and token claims, reply with the affected request IDs, approximate timestamps (including timezone), and non-sensitive token metadata such as the `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`, and `kid` values. Please do not send the JWT itself or any signing secret. Our support team can review the details.

Best,
{{agent_name}}

## Internal use

Keep this on the normal API v2 support route. Leo owns the first technical read when logs or the API contract are unclear. Do not imply an Atlas/platform incident or changed JWT behavior. Escalate beyond support/docs only if technical review finds evidence of a verification-code defect; involve product on priority/sequencing only if there is actual product work.
